questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I always wanted to live in Italy.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not easy in the beginning. the website can be a bit confusing in the beginning. Information came pr e-mail very late (one-two weeks before starting - very Italian, so be patient), but this information on e-mail was very helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not much actually. Only information e-mails, and the responses to all the e-mails I sent the counselor with questions :) No introweek or anything like it - but it was okay.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Quite difficult bc I was out too late. Therefore I found quite expensive housing. If you want to find off-campus housing, find it at least 2 months before you need it. There is a lot of websites that make it easier to find something, and with much more security than by going through private persons.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It can be expensive. Don't be afraid of living far from the city-center! It is actually nice. Living off-campus you have the opportunity to have your own private room. You can live with all sorts of people who may or may not be students like yourself.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I wanted to live on-campus, but was way too late to register apparently - information was nowhere to find of how early you had to register. So if you want on-campus just register as soon as possible.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I got information of the registration process in e-mail a little week before starting. Don't stress about it - you can try a lot of courses out the first couple of weeks and then register afterwards. Also, it is possible to change the registration as much as you want.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: E-mail with counselor.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I had all the classes I wanted. As far as I know, there wasn't any restrictions on how many could register into a course.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try different course out the first two weeks before you decide. Fx. Compare workload and exams.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was much easier than on UCPH. I was a BA student taking MA courses and was able to get high evaluations quite easily. Also It was possible to take courses from a completely different program than my own and still follow up.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Only lectures, no seminars and discussions as we have a lot of in UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Contemporary American Literature 9, Behavioural Sociology 9, Human Development and Mobility in a Changing World 9, Immersive stories and memories: From visual arts to video games 3.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Almost all of them actually. Human Development is very relevant if you're an anthropology student, it is a small class with a very interesting syllabus on migration. American Literature had a very compatible and nice teacher - I liked having some courses a outside of my own study. Immersive stories was arts and philosophy workshop: very reflective, fun and interesting.

Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *

Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: A lot of the text I had to read was online, so I didn't spend much on books. Drinks were less expensive than expected :)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There probably was some social or sports club on campus, we, as exchange student just never got information about it.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Theres was though an Erasmus-student-thing called ESN who planned a lot of social things - also some sports nights and parties.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go on museums, eat out on cute restaurants, walks in the beautiful parks... Explore the areas outside of the city center.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: So many things to see and do ^

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy. Traffic is crazy though - especially if you bike :)

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The easy going and non-busyness of everything. It is okay to be a little late sometimes and not talking everything so serious. Taking time to sit in bars for many many hours.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be patient and don't stress - information will come and everything is just chill once you get started. Explore the city, it has many nice areas. Don't stress about being social all the time - do what you like to.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You need a fiscal code (tax-number) - write an e-mail to the Italian embassy in Denmark.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To experience a way less study-stressing environment than in UCPH. To try different study-areas out. To find really close friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The beginning of of it all - to plan the trip, find housing, answering to all of the things in mobility-online, communicating with the host-institution - was confusing, but once you get through that all is good.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
